pr_title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Handle edge cases around CPU MinShares
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

For CPU requests between 0-2m, the Kubelet always configures 2 CPU shares (on linux). This causes some problems when pod resize code compares desired & actual resources.

This PR special cases CPU Request comparisons to consider any value <= 2m / 2 CPU shares to be equivalent.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114123
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126195

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This PR supersedes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120791

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
NONE
```

/sig node
/priority important-soon
/milestone v1.32
/assign @yujuhong

issue_context.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Minimum CPU request is displayed when only memory request is configured
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

If `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` is enabled and only a memory resource request is configured in a pod, the minimum CPU request set internally is displayed in the pod status:
```
$ kubectl get pod testpod -o jsonpath='spec: {.spec.containers[0].resources}{"\nallocatedResources: "}{.status.containerStatuses[0].allocatedResources}{"\nstatus: "}{.status.containerStatuses[0].resources}{"\n"}'
spec: {"requests":{"memory":"200Mi"}}
allocatedResources: {"memory":"200Mi"}
status: {"requests":{"cpu":"2m","memory":"200Mi"}}
```


### What did you expect to happen?

The minimum CPU request is not displayed in the pod status.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Enables the `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` feature.
2. Create a pod where only memory request is configured:
   <Details>

   ```
   apiVersion: v1
   kind: Pod
   metadata:
     labels:
       run: testpod
     name: testpod
   spec:
     containers:
     - image: nginx
       name: testpod
       resources:
         requests:
           memory: 200Mi
     restartPolicy: Always
   ```

   </Details>
3. See its resources in the pod status:
   ```
   $ kubectl get pod testpod -o jsonpath='spec: {.spec.containers[0].resources}{"\nallocatedResources: "}{.status.containerStatuses[0].allocatedResources}{"\nstatus: "}{.status.containerStatuses[0].resources}{"\n"}'
   spec: {"requests":{"memory":"200Mi"}}
   allocatedResources: {"memory":"200Mi"}
   status: {"requests":{"cpu":"2m","memory":"200Mi"}}
   ```



### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

comments: If `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` is disabled, will the internally set minimum CPU request be displayed in the Pod status?
No, container resources are not displayed in a pod status unless `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` is enabled.

This minimum CPU request in runtime status causes another error internally in kubelet. The following messages are logged in `kubelet.log` at every pod resync:
```
Jul 30 09:14:47 kind-control-plane kubelet[702]: I0730 09:14:47.436195     702 kuberuntime_manager.go:1051] "computePodActions got for pod" podActions="KillPod: false, CreateSandbox: false, UpdatePodResources: false, Attempt: 0, InitContainersToStart: [], ContainersToStart: [], EphemeralContainersToStart: [],ContainersToUpdate: map[cpu:[{0 {containerd 34bd8427f9d86a8795ba5d56ddc5f51d7b3dd9722686c62d30c1e672d6910ca9} {314572800 209715200 0 0} 0xc0014c7e00}]], ContainersToKill: map[]" pod="default/resize-pod"
Jul 30 09:14:47 kind-control-plane kubelet[702]: E0730 09:14:47.436340     702 kuberuntime_manager.go:750] "podResources.CPUQuota or podResources.CPUShares is nil" pod="resize-pod"
```

Because the unset CPU request in the pod spec is treated as zero and the CPU request in the runtime status is the minimum value, a resize action is computed due to the gap:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0fc167103189a4d462c3cc7a17b360c3d998f4bf/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go#L573
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0fc167103189a4d462c3cc7a17b360c3d998f4bf/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go#L586

This is the situation described in #126388 where the CPU request is resized when the CPU limit is not configured. Then, it hits the following error:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0fc167103189a4d462c3cc7a17b360c3d998f4bf/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go#L754-L758
The problem additionally mentioned (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126195#issuecomment-2257922410) may be fixed by #120791.

I have added a fix for the problem(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126195#issuecomment-2257922410) to the PR #126196 because this problem will occur more possibly especially if #126480 is merged. With #126480, this problem will occur in every `BestEffort` Qos pod.

@hshiina i followed steps in description using v1.32.0-alpha.0.191+1e45c3acd639c6 output is as you describe, interestingly 
testing it with https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123319 (v1.32.0-alpha.0.189+c897550e76e691), output is below.
```
kubectl get pod testpod -o jsonpath='spec: {.spec.containers[0].resources}{"\nallocatedResources: "}{.status.containerStatuses[0].allocatedResources}{"\nstatus: "}{.status.containerStatuses[0].resources}{"\n"}'
spec: {"requests":{"memory":"200Mi"}}
allocatedResources: 
status: 
```
+1 to accept this for triage, @kannon92 I added this in today's SIG Node agenda to decide triaging this

It's not clear to me that this is undesirable. The resources in the container status represent the "actual resources" that the container is currently configured with. If the Kubelet is setting a default CPU request, wouldn't this be a good place to surface it?

I'm afraid I misunderstood this problem.
`MilliCPUToShares()` returns `2` if `0`  is passed:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1a16c2d57815b013f11011897043dfa3ad463d76/pkg/kubelet/cm/helpers_linux.go#L84-L90
However, `sharesToMilliCPU()` returns `2` if `2` is passed:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1a16c2d57815b013f11011897043dfa3ad463d76/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/helpers_linux.go#L65-L69

`sharesToMilliCPU()` should convert `2 CPUshares` to `0 milliCPU` request.

review_comments: Considering that `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` is about to enter the beta stage, is it worth adding an API-level warning for this scenario? Or adding a warning log in the kubelet to notify users?
This seems like an optimization that we can also do without. Any strong reason to keep it?

This always gets corrected on the next sync loop, but that could be 1 minute later. That means that the resize InProgress status actually resolves more slowly when it's not making any changes than when it is (since we wouldn't set a WatchCondition in this case)

Hmm...we could also set the watch condition as an alternative. Just wanted to think about options before adding more special cases. Let's make it clear in the comment that this is an optimization and dropping it will only result in slower convergence.
Add a comment here to explain why we exclude those values.
